```{r}
# Setup for packages, data, quarter dates, and the predictor matrix
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)
library(prophet)

growth <- vroom::vroom("../DATA/CompanyGrowth.csv") %>%
	arrange(Year, Qrtr) %>%
	mutate(ds = as.Date(paste(Year, (Qrtr - 1) * 3 + 2, "15", sep = "-")))

X <- model.matrix(
	~ Income + Production + Savings + Unemployment,
	data = growth
)[, -1]
preds <- c("Income", "Production", "Savings", "Unemployment")
```

## Our approach

- Our current model predicts quarterly growth from four economic indicators.
- We tested two alternatives to see if they could project better.
- They help a little, and all three projections tell the same story.

## Our current model

![](model_equation.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

- The model is one line per quarter, four indicators in and growth out.
- It is fit on 198 quarters from 1976 to mid-2025 and explains about 77% of the variation in growth.
- To project a quarter, we plug that quarter's indicator values into the equation.

## How the current model performs {.smaller .scrollable}

```{r}
# Current multiple regression on all available quarters
current_lm <- lm(
	PctGrowth ~ Income + Production + Savings + Unemployment,
	data = growth
)

# Recent-history fit of the last 10 years of actual vs fitted growth
fit_plot <- ggplot(
	data.frame(
		Time = growth$Year + (growth$Qrtr - 1) / 4,
		Actual = growth$PctGrowth,
		Fitted = fitted(current_lm)
	) %>% filter(Time >= 2015),
	aes(x = Time)
) +
	geom_line(aes(y = Actual), color = "#2F5D62", linewidth = 1) +
	geom_line(aes(y = Fitted), color = "#D16B45", linewidth = 0.9) +
	labs(x = NULL, y = "Quarterly growth (%)") +
	theme_minimal()

fit_plot
```

- The fitted line tracks actual growth closely over the last decade.
- Its predictions were off by about 0.19 points per quarter on the last four quarters.
- Under this model, Q3 projects to 0.81% and Q4 to 0.70%.
- It cannot project a quarter unless the indicator values already exist.

## Why we tested alternatives {.scrollable}

```{r}
# Residual checks on the current model for variance, normality,
# and whether quarters are actually independent of each other
diagnostics <- data.frame(
	Check = c("Constant variance", "Normal errors", "Independent quarters"),
	p_value = c(
		lmtest::bptest(current_lm)$p.value,
		ks.test(MASS::stdres(current_lm), "pnorm", mean = 0, sd = 1)$p.value,
		Box.test(residuals(current_lm), lag = 8, type = "Ljung-Box")$p.value
	)
)
knitr::kable(diagnostics, digits = 3, col.names = c("Check", "p-value"))
```

- Every check we ran on the model's errors came back showing a problem.
- The big one is that quarters are correlated, and that correlation is what a time series model can take advantage of.

## Alternative 1, regression with time-aware errors {.scrollable}

- This keeps the same equation but lets the errors follow a seasonal ARIMA pattern.
- A bad quarter now carries information into the next projection.
- auto.arima selected an ARIMA(2,1,1)(1,0,1)[4] structure for the errors.

```{r}
# Regression with ARIMA errors where auto.arima picks the error structure
growth_ts <- ts(growth$PctGrowth, frequency = 4, start = c(1976, 1))
arima_reg <- auto.arima(y = growth_ts, xreg = X)

coef(arima_reg)
```

## Alternative 2, Prophet with the same indicators {.smaller .scrollable}

- Prophet draws a smooth trend plus a seasonal curve through the growth history.
- We feed it the same four indicators as extra inputs.
- It is built for forecasting, so it handles the calendar directly.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.5

# Prophet with the four indicators added as regressors
growth_prophet <- prophet()
for (r in preds) {
	growth_prophet <- add_regressor(growth_prophet, r)
}
growth_prophet <- fit.prophet(
	growth_prophet,
	data.frame(ds = growth$ds, y = growth$PctGrowth, growth[, preds])
)

# Prophet fit on the last 10 years, same view as the current model
prophet_plot <- ggplot(
	data.frame(
		Time = growth$Year + (growth$Qrtr - 1) / 4,
		Actual = growth$PctGrowth,
		Fitted = predict(growth_prophet, growth[, c("ds", preds)])$yhat
	) %>% filter(Time >= 2015),
	aes(x = Time)
) +
	geom_line(aes(y = Actual), color = "#2F5D62", linewidth = 1) +
	geom_line(aes(y = Fitted), color = "#D16B45", linewidth = 0.9) +
	labs(x = NULL, y = "Quarterly growth (%)") +
	theme_minimal()

prophet_plot
```

## Head to head, which predicts best? {.smaller .scrollable}

```{r}
# Holdout where we train each model through 2024 Q2, predict the last
# four quarters, and compare typical error
test_i <- growth$Year > 2024 | (growth$Year == 2024 & growth$Qrtr >= 3)

lm_hold <- lm(
	PctGrowth ~ Income + Production + Savings + Unemployment,
	data = growth[!test_i, ]
)
pred_lm <- predict(lm_hold, newdata = growth[test_i, ])

arima_reg_hold <- Arima(
	ts(growth$PctGrowth[!test_i], frequency = 4, start = c(1976, 1)),
	model = arima_reg, xreg = X[!test_i, ]
)
pred_reg <- forecast(arima_reg_hold, xreg = X[test_i, ])$mean

prophet_hold <- prophet()
for (r in preds) {
	prophet_hold <- add_regressor(prophet_hold, r)
}
prophet_hold <- fit.prophet(
	prophet_hold,
	data.frame(ds = growth$ds[!test_i], y = growth$PctGrowth[!test_i],
			   growth[!test_i, preds])
)
pred_ph <- predict(
	prophet_hold,
	data.frame(ds = growth$ds[test_i], growth[test_i, preds])
)$yhat

rmse <- function(actual, pred) sqrt(mean((actual - pred)^2))
holdout_rmse <- data.frame(
	Model = c("Current regression", "Regression + ARIMA errors", "Prophet"),
	RMSE = c(
		rmse(growth$PctGrowth[test_i], pred_lm),
		rmse(growth$PctGrowth[test_i], as.numeric(pred_reg)),
		rmse(growth$PctGrowth[test_i], pred_ph)
	)
)

rmse_plot <- ggplot(holdout_rmse, aes(x = RMSE, y = reorder(Model, -RMSE))) +
	geom_col(fill = c("#999999", "#2F5D62", "#999999"), width = 0.6) +
	labs(x = "Prediction error (percentage points)", y = NULL) +
	theme_minimal()

rmse_plot
```

- On the last four quarters the errors were 0.18 for the ARIMA model, 0.19 for the current model, and 0.20 for Prophet.
- It is a tight race, but the time-aware errors come out ahead.

## How we get Q3 and Q4 projections {.scrollable}

```{r}
# Prophet model for each indicator, forecast to the end of 2025
# (two quarters, Q3 and Q4)
future_ds <- data.frame(ds = as.Date(c("2025-08-15", "2025-11-15")))

future_X <- sapply(preds, function(v) {
	pm <- prophet(data.frame(ds = growth$ds, y = growth[[v]]))
	predict(pm, future_ds)$yhat
})
colnames(future_X) <- preds
future_indicators <- cbind(Quarter = c("Q3", "Q4"), as.data.frame(future_X))

knitr::kable(future_indicators, row.names = FALSE, digits = 2)
```

- The Q3 and Q4 indicator values do not exist yet, so we forecast them too.
- Each indicator gets its own Prophet model, projected two quarters out.
- Every model then uses the same projected inputs.

## What the rest of 2025 looks like {.scrollable}

```{r}
# Final projections for Q3-Q4 2025 using the forecasted indicators
future_df <- cbind(future_ds, as.data.frame(future_X))

proj_table <- data.frame(
	Quarter = c("Q3", "Q4"),
	"Current regression" = predict(current_lm, newdata = future_df),
	"Regression + ARIMA" = as.numeric(forecast(arima_reg, xreg = future_X)$mean),
	"Prophet" = predict(growth_prophet, future_df)$yhat,
	check.names = FALSE
) %>%
	mutate(across(-Quarter, ~ sprintf("%.2f%%", .x)))

knitr::kable(proj_table)
```

- All three models project growth between 0.57% and 0.81% per quarter.
- The preferred model says about 0.7% in both quarters.

## What actually drives VistaLux growth {.smaller .scrollable}

```{r}
# Coefficients from the preferred model (regression + ARIMA errors)
# showing how much each indicator moves quarterly growth
drivers <- data.frame(
	Indicator = preds,
	Effect = coef(arima_reg)[preds]
)

driver_plot <- ggplot(
	drivers,
	aes(x = Effect, y = reorder(Indicator, Effect), fill = Effect > 0)
) +
	geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
	scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.1)) +
	labs(x = "Effect on quarterly growth (percentage points)", y = NULL) +
	theme_minimal()

driver_plot
```

- Income dominates, with one extra point of income growth worth about 0.74 points for us.
- Unemployment and savings pull growth down, while production helps a little.
- We are a discretionary-goods company, so this pattern tracks.

## Recommendation

- We recommend the regression with ARIMA errors because it did the best job predicting the recent quarters.
- The rest of 2025 should see steady growth around 0.7% a quarter.
- Income is the number to watch going forward.
